To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
data driven choices for regularization parameters yield estimator performance that is uniformly close to that of the best (unfeasible, data dependent) choice of regularization parameter.

(i) the risk of a regularized estimator is a function of the true data generating process, (ii) a data driven choice of regularization parameter yields an estimator that is uniformly close in risk to the risk attained by the optimal choice of regularization parameters, and (iii) in empirical economics, the optimal choice of regularized estimations is often a ridge or lasso estimator.

(i) regularized estimation methods are useful tools in empirical economics; (ii) data driven choices of the regularization parameters are useful in empirical economics; and (iii) data driven choices are useful even in settings where the data generating process is known to belong to a parametric family.

, for many empirical settings, regularized estimators with data driven regularization parameters have risk that is uniformly close to the best possible risk.
